blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Objectives: Patient portal messages provide invaluable information about communication dynamics between patients and healthcare providers, but extracting it manually is labor-intensive. We developed and evaluated EPPC-CARE, an automated framework for identifying communication behaviors together with the supporting text for each classification. Materials and Methods: From 867 messages, we obtained 5,516 reference standard annotations. Each annotation is a triplet of communication-related text (span), a broader communication category (Code), and a specific subcategory (Sub-code). We evaluated EPPC-CARE's identified triplets across six open-weight large language models (LLMs) against supervised fine-tuning and communication-based models such as EPPC-OASIS. We also compared EPPC-CARE with human expert annotations on 100 messages. Results: EPPC-CARE improved performance over EPPC-OASIS across all six models. EPPC-CARE's Triplet F1 improved by 2.90 percentage points on average, with a best score of 64.4%. On the human expert evaluation subset, EPPC-CARE and the human expert showed comparable agreement with the reference standard, with differences favoring EPPC-CARE. Discussion: These findings suggest that identifying triplet components (span, code, subcode) sequentially can improve performance across model families while preserving the supporting text behind each identification. EPPC-CARE links the communication code and subcode with the source text (span), supporting human verification of automated annotations in clinical informatics. EPPC-CARE may therefore make larger-scale studies of patient-provider communication more feasible and provide a foundation for human-in-the-loop annotation workflows. Conclusion: EPPC-CARE offers a more reliable and reviewable approach for automated characterization of communication behaviors in secure patient-provider messaging.
blocks.zh: 目标:病人门户网站信息提供有关病人与保健提供者之间交流动态的宝贵信息,但人工提取信息需要劳动密集型。 我们开发并评价了EPPC-CARE,这是一个自动框架,用于识别通信行为,以及每种分类的辅助文本。 材料和方法: 从867条信息中,我们获得了5,516个参考标准说明. 每条注释是通信相关文本(span),更广泛的通信类别(Code)和特定的子类别(Sub-code)的三重音. 我们对照EPPC-OASIS等有监督的微调和通信模式,评估了EPPC-CARE在6个开放量大语言模型(LLMs)中确定的三重体. 我们还将EPPC-CARE与关于100条信息的人类专家说明相比较。 成果:在六个模式中,欧洲石油伙伴关系中心-欧洲石油伙伴关系中心的业绩都比欧洲石油伙伴关系中心-美洲组织信息系统有所改善。 EPPC-CARE的Triplet F1平均改进2.90个百分点,最佳得分64.4%. 在人类专家评价子集方面,EPPC-CARE和人类专家表现出与参考标准相当的一致,不同的是赞成EPPC-CARE。 讨论: 这些调查结果表明,相继确定三重元件(span,代码,子代码)可以改善各模范家族的性能,同时保留每次识别背后的支持文本. EPPC-CARE将通信代码和子代码与源文本(span)相连接,支持临床信息学中自动注释的人类验证. 因此,EPPC-CARE可以使更大规模地研究病人与提供者之间的沟通更为可行,并为人与人之间的通知工作流程提供基础。 结论:EPPC-CARE为在安全的病人-提供者信息传递中自动描述通信行为提供了一个更可靠和可审查的方法。

blocks.en: Supplementary material
blocks.zh: 补充材料

blocks.en: The Appendix (Supplementary Material) accompanying this preprint provides supplementary methodological details, benchmark characteristics (Supplementary Table S1), comparison-system configurations (Supplementary Table S2), task-specific training settings (Supplementary Table S3), complete cross-model micro-F1 results (Supplementary Table S4), the matched inference-efficiency evaluation (Supplementary Section S1, Table S5), sensitivity analyses for Span matching, annotation assignment, and Span length (Supplementary Section S2, Tables S6–S7), and the cross-model precision and recall breakdown comparing EPPC-CARE against SFT (Supplementary Section S3, Tables S8–S10).
blocks.zh: 本预印本所附附录(补充材料)提供了补充方法细节、基准特征(补充表S1)、比较系统配置(补充表S2)、任务特定培训环境(补充表S3)、完整的跨模型微型F1结果(补充表S4)、相应的推算效率评价(补充部分S1、表S5)、Span比对、注释任务和Span长度(补充部分S2、表S6-S7)的敏感性分析,以及将EPPC-CARE与SFT(补充部分S3、表S8-S10)相比较的跨模型精度和召回细目。

blocks.en: Ethics statement
blocks.zh: 道德操守说明

blocks.en: This study used an existing de-identified benchmark derived from secure patient–provider messages collected at Yale New Haven Hospital. The underlying secure-message data source was collected under approval of the Yale New Haven Hospital Institutional Review Board, as reported in prior work from this research program. 50 The present study was a secondary analysis of de-identified data; no direct patient identifiers were available to the investigators conducting this analysis. The data remained within the institutionally governed computing environment used for the EPPCMinerBen research program.
blocks.zh: 这项研究使用了从耶鲁·纽黑文医院收集的安全病人-提供者信息中得出的现有非识别基准。 基础的安全信息数据来源是在耶鲁·纽黑文医院机构审查委员会的批准下收集的,本研究方案先前的工作对此作了报告。 50 本研究报告是对已查明身份的数据的二级分析;进行这种分析的调查员没有直接的病人识别资料。 这些数据仍然停留在用于环管中心本研究方案的机构化计算环境中。

blocks.en: Data and code availability
blocks.zh: 数据和代码的可用性

blocks.en: The clinical message corpus cannot be publicly released because of institutional privacy and data-governance restrictions. Source code, prompts, training configurations, and evaluation scripts will be made publicly available upon publication, without patient message text.
blocks.zh: 由于机构隐私和数据治理的限制,临床信息包不能公开发布。 原始代码、提示、培训配置和评价脚本将在出版后公开,不提供病人信息文本。
